dedupe_keys.name: moose multiphysics object oriented simulation environment

description: MOOSE, the Multiphysics Object-Oriented Simulation Environment, is a finite-element multiphysics framework developed mainly by Idaho National Laboratory, with Argonne, Los Alamos and Oak Ridge national laboratories listed as authoring institutions in the INL software catalogue. It gives a high-level C++ interface to nonlinear solver technology (PETSc) and is fully coupled, fully implicit and automatically parallel, with the README citing runs on more than 100,000 CPU cores, built-in mesh adaptivity, continuous and discontinuous Galerkin methods, multiscale solves and about 30 pluggable interfaces. Applications built on it include BISON for nuclear fuel and Griffin for radiation transport and reactor multiphysics. The code is open source under the GNU LGPL 2.1 and free of charge on GitHub, with dated releases (the latest tag read was 2025-09-05-release) and commits up to 14 September 2026. Coverage is general, with a strong nuclear engineering focus. Caveats: MOOSE is a framework, so users build or obtain an application for their physics, and large runs need parallel computing resources. Simulation uses are coupled thermal, mechanical and neutronic simulation of reactors and fuel under accident and hazard loads. Related records: model-cardinal couples NekRS and OpenMC within MOOSE, and model-openmc is a Monte Carlo transport code used with it.
